preamble: The voiced dental/alveolar stop /d/ becomes the voiced palatal stop [ɟ] under the influence of a neighbouring palatal or as a regional palatalization of long dentals. In Hungarian, /d/ takes the palatal place of a following gy /ɟ/ across morpheme boundaries (partial palatal assimilation, optional in careful speech). In Central and Northern Norwegian dialects the historically long dental dd is palatalized, reaching a palatal stop [ɟː] in words such as fadder. The change is regional and confined to a few languages.

examples.note: Partial palatal assimilation: /d/ takes the palatal place of the following gy, giving a geminate [ɟː]; the parallel t + gy gives [ɟː] in nemzetgyűlés.
Palatalization of long dentals north of the Oslo–Bergen isogloss; descriptions range from palatalized [dʲ] to a full palatal stop [ɟː].
